User.title: User
User.description: Represents an application user with role and hierarchy information.

role.description: The role of the user within the application.

reportsTo.description: The UID of the user this user reports to (e.g., a vendedor reports to a supervisor).

CustomerProfile.title: CustomerProfile
CustomerProfile.description: Represents a customer's profile, including contact information, preferences, and purchase history.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer Profile.

purchaseHistory.description: List of previous purchases (references to Sales records).

FollowUpActivity.title: FollowUpActivity
FollowUpActivity.description: Represents a follow-up activity with a customer (call, email, meeting).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Follow-Up Activity.

activityType.description: Type of activity (e.g., call, email, meeting).

TaskReminder.title: TaskReminder
TaskReminder.description: Represents a reminder for a task (e.g., follow-up call, appointment).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task Reminder.

taskType.description: Type of task (e.g., follow-up call, appointment).

isCompleted.description: Indicates whether the task is completed.

SalesFunnelStatus.title: SalesFunnelStatus
SalesFunnelStatus.description: Represents the status of a customer in the sales funnel.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Sales Funnel Status.

status.description: Current status in the sales funnel (e.g., Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support the Meny Back-Office application for managing customer profiles, follow-up activities, task reminders, and sales funnel status. It prioritizes authorization independence, clarity, and scalability, following the core design principles outlined in the prompt. Specifically, it leverages path-based ownership and avoids `get()` calls in security rules to ensure atomic operations.

Authorization Independence is achieved by structuring data so that authorization depends only on the `request.auth.uid` and the document path. For example, customer profiles and related data are stored under `/users/{userId}`, making ownership clear and enforceable without needing to read parent documents.

The structure also supports secure `list` operations (QAPs) by segregating data based on ownership.  Each salesperson's data is stored under their user ID, ensuring they can only list and access data they own. The use of path-based ownership and the avoidance of complex, hierarchical dependencies guarantees efficient and secure data access, simplifying security rule definitions and enhancing debuggability.
